edit.topology.notes: ground, inner race with shaft, outer race (bell) with shaft, cage, 6 balls; each ball contacts an inner groove, an outer groove and a cage window (18 higher pairs); cage to races are spherical sliding fits. The joint count (Kutzbach, 20) is not the mobility: each ball contact is counted as a point contact, while the groove holds the ball centre on a line, and each ball's spin is an idle freedom; the six balls with the two spherical fits overconstrain the cage. The true mobility is 1, solved in closed form by the homokinetic block.
edit.build.defining_relations: Balls lie in the homokinetic plane through J whose normal bisects the two shaft axes (tilted beta/2 from each); omega_out = omega_in; ball k sits on a circle of radius Rp in that plane where it meets inner groove k (near angle theta + 60k; it shifts a little round its window at an angle); each ball runs along its inner groove by ±Rp sin(beta/2) per turn.

review.note: Review against the record (not in the 2026-10-19 review). The principle is the conical pendulum: the faster the spin, the higher and wider the balls run, and the links lift the sleeve. The speed is the control (97.6 to 133.8 rpm, default 101.6); the arm angle follows from the balance h = g / omega^2, never sweeping by itself. A ball centre is traced, a horizontal circle, with ghost circles at both ends of the speed range, low and narrow against high and wide. The pendulum height h from the pivot down to the ball is dimensioned. The plot shows arm angle and sleeve height against speed. View near front elevation, slightly from above, so the circles read as flat ellipses and heights read true.
